story.headline: The dollar held near its highest since April 2025 before the Fed's meeting minutes at 1:00 PM CT, and gold fell below $3,800. The pound hit a one-month low as UK core inflation held steady.

reads.policy: A December Fed hike is now treated as all but certain, so the focus has moved to how many more follow next year. Steady UK core inflation trimmed bets on a second Bank of England hike, while firmer euro-area core prices keep a December European Central Bank hike on track. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.
reads.growth: US housing starts jumped in October, but permits for future building fell, a mixed sign for the US economy. Japan's record exports point to a pickup there. The US still looks firmer than most, which supports the dollar.
reads.inflation: UK inflation rose to 3.6% on fuel, but core prices held steady, so the pound lost some of its rate edge. Euro-area core inflation was revised up, backing a December hike there. Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes.
reads.risk: Nvidia's strong results calmed worries about tech stocks after two days of losses. Iran attacked a US base in Kuwait and ships in the Gulf, but markets took it in stride. The dollar stayed firm, and the Aussie and kiwi held near their lows.
reads.tot: Oil fell as US crude stocks rose, which takes a little away from the Canadian dollar and helps energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area. Gold's slide below $3,800 weighs on the Aussie, since Australia is a big gold producer.
reads.positioning: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.
reads.fiscal: The European Central Bank's stability report named France's debts as a risk and said cutting deficits is overdue, which keeps weighing on the euro. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs near 5%, which weighs a little on trust in the dollar.

fed.summary: The Federal Reserve held rates on October 28 with two officials voting to hike. Hot inflation and firm consumer spending have made a December hike all but certain and kept the dollar near its highest since April 2025.
fed.priced: December: hike all but certain, with a half-point move only a small chance. More hikes expected next year.
fed.why: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's 2% goal. New York Fed President John Williams says one more hike is probably needed, but nothing dramatic.
fed.watch: Minutes of the October meeting Wednesday, November 18 at 1:00 PM CT, then weekly jobless claims Thursday, November 19 at 7:30 AM CT. The decision is December 9.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada raised rates to 2.50% in October and said more may be needed. October inflation held at 3.1% with core prices near 2%, so a December hike now looks less likely than not.
boc.priced: December: hold more likely, with a hike a bit under even odds.
boc.why: Energy is lifting headline inflation, but core prices are calm and the economy is shedding jobs, so the bank can afford to wait.
boc.watch: Canada's November jobs figures on December 4 and the path of oil prices. The decision is December 9.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand held at 2.75% in October in a narrow vote. Rising unemployment has made a December hike less certain, and the kiwi has fallen to its lowest since 2020.
rbnz.priced: December: hike possible but not fully expected.
rbnz.why: Inflation pressures argue for a hike, but unemployment at its highest since 2015 argues for waiting. Businesses' inflation expectations barely moved and dairy prices were flat at the latest auction.
rbnz.watch: Governor Anna Breman speaks Wednesday, November 18 at 12:00 PM CT. The decision is December 9.

ecb.summary: The European Central Bank held at 2.50% in October and a December hike is widely expected. Final figures confirmed euro-area inflation at 4.0% with core prices revised up, but the euro has slipped below $1.10 as US rates rise faster.
ecb.priced: December: hike widely expected, possibly the last for a while.
ecb.why: Euro-area inflation is about double the bank's goal and core prices are firming. Weak factories and France's debts, which the bank's stability report singled out, limit how far it can go.
ecb.watch: President Christine Lagarde speaks Wednesday, November 18 at 8:25 AM CT. The decision is December 17.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, far below other major banks, and is expected to hike in December. Governor Kazuo Ueda says rates will keep rising and warns that the weak yen is lifting food prices.
boj.why: The weak yen is pushing import costs and food prices up, and record chip exports show the economy can take higher rates. The small summer contraction is the main reason to wait.
boj.watch: Whether Japan buys yen if the dollar tops 160 again, and Governor Kazuo Ueda's speech on November 30. The decision is December 18.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates to 4.85% on November 3, the highest among the major banks, in a six-to-three vote. Big Australian banks think that is the peak, though pay rose a bit faster than forecast in the third quarter.
rba.priced: December: a hold expected, with rates seen at their peak.
rba.why: Most board members worry inflation is too high, and faster pay growth backs them. Three feared a sharper slowdown, and unemployment is at a five-year high.
rba.watch: October jobs figures Wednesday, November 18 at 6:30 PM CT. The decision is December 8.

boe.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% on November 5 and said more may follow. UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October, but steady core prices trimmed bets on a second hike in December, which is still seen as likely.
boe.priced: December: a second hike more likely than not.
boe.why: High fuel costs from the Middle East conflict keep UK inflation near twice the bank's goal. Core prices held steady, though, which gives the bank less reason to hurry.
boe.watch: Governor Andrew Bailey speaks Wednesday, November 18 at 9:00 AM CT, and UK retail sales follow Friday, November 20 at 1:00 AM CT. The decision is December 17.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero and can sell francs if they get too strong. Low Swiss inflation means no hike is in sight.
snb.why: Swiss inflation is low, so the bank has no reason to raise rates and some room to cut if the franc climbs.
snb.watch: Any flare-up that sends money into the franc. The decision is December 10.

USD.summary: The dollar sits third on the board. High US interest rates support it, while large budget deficits weigh a little. With a December Fed hike seen as near certain, it is near its highest since April 2025.

EUR.summary: The euro sits fifth, just below the middle of the board. Cheaper oil helps the euro area, but France's debts and rates below most of the others hold it back. Rising US rates have pushed it just under $1.10, its lowest since April 2025.

GBP.summary: The pound sits at the top of the board, a whisker ahead of the Aussie, because UK interest rates are among the highest of the eight. Steady UK core inflation trimmed bets on a December hike and pushed it to a one-month low.

JPY.summary: The yen sits second from the bottom because Japanese interest rates are far below the others and inflation is close to the Bank of Japan's goal. A likely December rate hike and warnings from Japan's finance minister only just keep the dollar below 160 yen.

CHF.summary: The franc sits at the bottom of the board. Swiss interest rates are the lowest of the eight and inflation is too low to need higher rates. The dollar has climbed to its highest against it in about 18 months.

AUD.summary: The Aussie sits second on the board, just behind the pound, thanks to the highest interest rates among the major central banks. Faster pay growth supports it, but gold's slide below $3,800 has kept it near its lowest since January.

CAD.summary: The Canadian dollar sits sixth, in the lower half of the board. Falling oil prices hurt Canada's exports, and recent Canadian data has mostly missed forecasts. The US dollar is close to its October high against it.

NZD.summary: The kiwi sits fourth, in the middle of the board. Firm prices for New Zealand's dairy exports help, but doubts over a December rate hike have kept it close to its lowest since 2020.
